summary: Odd 5xx wave from ingress websocket fanout causing upstream runtime GPU watchdog timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (initial report: ThinkInk Labs) observed a short-lived but high-rate 5xx spike on websocket-based routes between 2026-03-13T08:10Z and 2026-03-13T08:27Z. Errors surface as HTTP 502/503 from the api-gateway; upstream runtime instances report GPU watchdog timeouts and rapid process restarts.

Impact: Intermittent failures for streaming/chat sessions for ThinkInk Labs (dedicated cluster). Estimated ~80% of websocket sessions opened during the window failed to establish or dropped mid-stream. No data loss reported but significant UX disruption for the customer.

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for ThinkInk Labs, model variants pinned to gpt-backend-v1. Autoscaling disabled for dedicated pool (customer preference).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open 40 concurrent websocket streaming sessions that immediately send a 1–2 token handshake followed by a short prompt.
2) Maintain steady creation rate of ~6 connections/sec for 3 minutes.
3) Observe ~30–70% session drop / 502 return from API gateway after a few seconds.

Observed logs & outputs:
- api-gateway logs: repeated upstream "502 Bad Gateway" with upstream reset / connection refused.
- ingress-sidecar: connection spike + "accept queue full" traces around 08:12Z.
- runtime logs on affected instances: repeated "GPU watchdog timeout: kernel stalled" and immediate process SIGABRT/restart.
- Prometheus traces: runtime per-process GPU utilization near 98–100% with kernel preemption events; per-request latency spikes before watchdog.

Customer notes: The workload is websocket-first small-handshake, then short generation. Customer asserts this pattern used to be supported at this scale until last week (they have unchanged client behavior).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-13 08:20Z — Triage: Support triaged to SRE. Correlated api-gateway 502s with runtime watchdog alerts on the dedicated cluster.

Timeline & correlation:
- 08:10–08:12Z: incoming websocket connection rate increased (ThinkInk warmup).
- 08:12Z: ingress-sidecar accept-queue growth; api-gateway begins to return 502s as upstream sockets refuse.
- 08:12–08:18Z: affected runtime pids show GPU watchdog timeouts; nvml logs show repeated kernel preemption and driver recoveries.

Hypotheses considered:
- H1: sudden fanout of websocket handshakes is saturating runtime event loop and triggering kernel watchdog on GPUs due to synchronous prefetch/initialization path.
- H2: ingress-sidecar accept-queue pressure is causing many half-open handshakes, which amplify latency and cause them to queue on a small set of warmed runtimes, producing hot GPU contention and watchdog timeouts.
- H3: a recent runtime library change (PR 1829) altered kernel launch parameters for small prompt shapes leading to less cooperative scheduling on our GPU drivers under high connection churn.

Evidence:
- Heatmap of requests -> small-sequence launches correlated to failed pids.
- Runtime stack traces show stalls inside memory allocation + cuBLAS init paths prior to watchdog.
- The rate of 5xx decreases when we artificially throttle ingress accept-rate or when we route websocket handshakes to a warm standby pool.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Lowered websocket accept rate at api-gateway layer for ThinkInk pool (reduces client concurrency). Result: immediate reduction in watchdog hits and 5xx.
- Applied local routing to shift new handshakes to warm standby runtimes with prewarmed KV cache; reduced per-runtime burst.

Next steps planned:
- Roll back or patch runtime PR 1829 in a testbed to measure kernel launch behavior under websocket churn.
- Implement a long-term fix: move init/prefetch off hot GPU thread or add a cooperative init path for small handshake prompts.
- Add an ingress-sidecar backpressure metric alert and an automated soft-rate-limit for websocket handshake fanout.
comments: Priya Shah (2026-03-13T09:02Z): Logged initial customer report and collected websocket traces + api-gateway logs. Added SRE oncall. Marking as P1 due to customer impact.

Jordan Kim (SRE) (2026-03-13T09:18Z): Correlated api-gateway 502s with runtime GPU watchdogs. I throttled handshake accept at the gateway for ThinkInk pool — error rate dropped immediately. Continuing investigation into runtime startup path.

Marta Alvarez (Runtime Eng) (2026-03-13T10:05Z): Noted PR 1829 changed cuBLAS workspace sizing on small token launches; reproducing locally with websocket-fanout harness. Suspect cooperative scheduling regression under heavy connection churn.

Customer (Anil Rao, ThinkInk Labs) (2026-03-13T10:30Z): We saw a 60% failure rate during our morning batch. Thank you for the throttle — can you confirm no data was lost? We prefer no broad rate limits but will accept temporary mitigation.

Jordan Kim (SRE) (2026-03-13T11:00Z): Confirmed no generation outputs lost — failing requests did not complete. Providing a short-lived retry guidance to client: exponential backoff starting at 250ms for handshake retries. Documented in ticket.

Marta Alvarez (Runtime Eng) (2026-03-13T14:20Z): Runbook item: add a soft prewarm path that performs cuBLAS init on a background thread before accepting a streaming handshake. Experiment scheduled in staging today.
Priya Shah (Support) (2026-03-14T02:10Z): Customer confirmed improved experience after gateway throttle; requesting ETA for permanent fix and whether we can disable the throttle after patch.
Jordan Kim (SRE) (2026-03-14T03:05Z): SRE to coordinate canary of patched runtime in staging, then promote to a subset of dedicated pools. Tentative ETA 48–72 hours pending test results.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: Gateway handshake-rate throttle for ThinkInk dedicated pool and routing new handshakes to a warm-standby runtime group. Immediate reduction in 5xx observed. Engineering hypothesis points to recent runtime PR 1829 affecting small-launch kernel behavior under connection churn.

Planned permanent fix: Implement background cooperative init for cuBLAS/cuDNN on handshake and test reverting PR 1829 variants. Add ingress-sidecar soft-backpressure and an automated handshake throttling mechanism.

Follow-up actions:
- Eng to run canary with patched runtime (assigned to Marta Alvarez).
- SRE to add new alert for websocket accept-queue growth and GPU watchdog rate (assigned to Jordan Kim).
- Support to coordinate customer communication and remove temporary throttle only after successful canary.
resolution_notes: Ongoing: mitigation successful; root cause not yet fully confirmed. Canary and postmortem to be scheduled. Customer updated and monitoring continues.
